newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares lose faith and slide lower.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares lose faith and slide lower.

text.p: Italian shares turned tail after a firmer start on Wednesday as Wall Street opened on a lower track and many individual shares ran out of steam in a generally lacklustre trading day after making gains earlier in the week.

Olivetti was supported early by talk Japanese groups NEC and Sony might be interested in buying its PC company and the shares rose to a high of 545 lire, but after both group's distanced themselves from the talk Olivetti shares slipped back to end off 1.76 percent at 518 lire.
The all-share Mibtel index ended off 0.5 percent at 9,948 while the blue chip Mib30 was 0.68 percent down at 14,945.
On the positive side, Fiat shares recovered from fresh year lows on Tuesday to end up 1.48 percent at 4,170 lire helped by the news that it was to invest $1 billion in India over the next five years.

Dealers said news Fiat was investing in joint ventures with local partners in a developing car market was seen a positive sign of the group's commitment to the automobile sector despite a continued depressed Italian car market.
Weighing on the market was ENI, off 0.71 percent at 7,395 lire, after the energy group's shares had risen this week after a smaller than expected second tranche offer.
Telecoms were weaker with STET off 0.25 percent at 5,200 lire and TIM down 0.98 percent at 3,235 lire and Telecom Italia 1.62 percent easier at 3,392 lire.
